system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s “negotiated”, “agreed” and “settled” characterisations do not evidence Buyer approval. In particular, no Amelia Frost approval has been given for either the 20% cap or 18-month period.

| ID / issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | **25% / AUD 6m** general Warranty cap. | **Reject and restore 25%.** The 20% fallback requires Amelia Frost’s prior written approval identifying this draft, which has not been given. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | **AUD 25,000** de minimis; **AUD 250,000** deductible basket, with only the excess recoverable. | **AUD 5,000** de minimis; **AUD 50,000** tipping basket, with recovery from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Reject and replace with Buyer thresholds.** Seller’s proposal materially reduces recovery through thresholds five times higher and a deductible rather than tipping basket. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | General Warranty Claims notified within **18 months**; limitations presumptively apply to all Claims. | **24 months** for general Warranty Claims, confined to that category. | **Reject and restore 24 months.** The 18-month fallback lacks required Amelia Frost approval, and the general limit must not govern other claim categories. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limit as general warranties. | Separate Fundamental/Title regime: **100% cap**, at least **six years**, and no general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar. | **Reject and create a separate regime.** Ownership, authority and capacity risks cannot appropriately be confined to 20% and 18 months. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no adequate fraud carve-out is identified. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of **all** caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum enforceable extent. | **Insert the full non-waivable carve-out.** Seller misconduct must not be protected by contractual limitations. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | Deemed general disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public corporate records. | Only matters **specifically and fairly disclosed**, with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope. | **Delete deemed/general disclosure.** A whole-data-room or public-search construct improperly transfers the Seller’s disclosure burden to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by the Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records. | Delete the blanket actual, adviser and constructive-knowledge exclusion; any warranty knowledge qualifier should use named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry and never affect title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Reject the qualifier.** It converts mere discoverability into knowledge and could neutralise warranties despite inadequate disclosure. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent, although no final consent or evidence of satisfaction of its conditions is supplied. | Before Completion, effective Bluefen consent **and evidence that all associated conditions are satisfied**. | **Make this a strict Completion condition.** Bluefen represents about AUD 3.6m/30% of FY26 revenue, so reasonable endeavours or bare delivery is insufficient. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** remains outstanding; security release to follow Completion. | Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective releases of all security at Completion. | **Reject the proposed post-Completion release.** Any deferred release would require an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval, neither of which is presently available. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | AUD **420,000** Completion bonuses are said to be a Seller matter but are omitted from the funds flow; on-costs are unaddressed. | Express Seller funding or a specific funds-flow line item for AUD 420,000 **plus any triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs**. | **Revise the funds flow and quantify on-costs.** Omission risks the Company—and economically the Buyer—bearing a Completion-triggered Seller liability. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; Seller regards it as adequate; DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open but this is not independently verified. | Broader indemnity covering losses arising from failure to obtain ownership/transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials, while preserving the payment/cure route under SOW3. | **Broaden the indemnity and verify payment status.** The risk is defective IP ownership and related loss, not merely the amount of one invoice, and AUD 180,000 is not independently confirmed. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Characterised as preliminary and not expected to be material; available material does not establish access, exact scope, notification duty or loss. | Preservation of logs and evidence, prompt investigation, continuing updates, cooperation and appropriate pre-/post-Completion covenants or protection based on verified findings. | **Require investigation protections without assuming an outcome.** The record supports neither a confirmed breach or notification duty nor dismissal of the incident as immaterial. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals—AUD **330,000** total—are asserted to be ordinary-course operating costs. | Assess timing, scope, termination rights, accrual and whether each commitment is unavoidable or ordinary course; no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction. | **Reserve treatment pending diligence.** The documents do not establish the Seller’s ordinary-course characterisation or justify automatic classification either way. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | General limitations are intended to apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded, potentially sweeping Tax, IP, payment, covenant and other claims into one regime. | Separate regimes for Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment obligations, covenants and specific indemnities, with express priority and no hidden general override. | **Rewrite the limitation architecture.** Distinct risks and negotiated remedies must not be unintentionally compressed into the general Warranty regime. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | Relies on the DD-012 internal share register as evidence of ownership of 100% of the shares. | Independent evidence of ownership, encumbrance status and authority, supported by originals/certified records, searches, releases and Completion deliverables as appropriate. | **Do not accept DD-012 as conclusive.** A Seller-supplied internal register identifies its asserted source but is not independent proof of good, unencumbered title. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says Tax and IP warranty positions are settled under the proposed general regime. | Treat both as **open**, negotiate their substantive warranties, indemnities, caps, periods and exclusions separately, and assume neither unlimited liability nor an agreed resolution. | **Reject the “settled” characterisation and reserve all rights.** No Buyer authority or verified agreement supports folding Tax and IP into the Seller’s general regime. |
=== END ADVICE ===
